title: Optimizing Acute Care Rehabilitation for Critically Ill Adults
official: Optimizing Acute Care Rehabilitation for Critically Ill Adults
summary:
The goal of this clinical trial is to determine the optimal frequency, duration, and timing of physical therapy (PT) and occupational therapy (OT) rehabilitation to improve physical and cognitive function in critically ill adults receiving mechanical ventilation in the intensive care unit (ICU).

The main questions it aims to answer are:

1. What combination of rehabilitation session frequency, session duration, and timing of OT initiation produces the greatest improvements in physical function and activities of daily living at hospital discharge and 3 months?
2. Which patient characteristics, including age and comorbidities, are associated with greater benefits from different rehabilitation approaches?

Researchers will compare eight combinations of rehabilitation strategies, varying three components:

Session frequency: 4 versus 7 days per week. Session duration: 20 versus 40 minutes per session. Timing of OT initiation: Early initiation (within 24 hours of randomization) versus delayed initiation (at ICU discharge or 7 days after randomization, whichever occurs later).

Participants will:

* Be randomly assigned to one of eight rehabilitation combinations.
* Receive individualized, progressive PT focused on strength, balance, mobility, and endurance, beginning within 24 hours of randomization.
* Receive individualized OT focused on daily activities, including grooming, bathing, dressing, and feeding, beginning according to their assigned group.
* Participate in rehabilitation sessions until hospital discharge, 21 days after randomization, or successful completion of predefined rehabilitation milestones, whichever occurs first.
* Undergo assessments of physical function, daily activities, and cognitive function during hospitalization and at hospital discharge.
* Complete a follow-up assessment 3 months after hospital discharge to evaluate physical and cognitive function, quality of life, mental health, and recovery.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* ICU patients age \>18 years.
* Mechanically ventilated for \<48 hours.
* Expected to require mechanical ventilation for \>24 hours at the time of randomization.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Pre-existing functional impairment defined as a Barthel score \<70.
* Pre-existing cognitive impairment using an IQCODE cutoff of 3.42.
* Acute brain pathology (e.g., traumatic brain injury, stroke) without exclusion for ICU-delirium.
* Proven or suspected spinal cord injury or neuromuscular disease that will result in permanent or prolonged weakness (without exclusion for ICU-acquired weakness) at time of eligibility.
* Has "bedrest" orders and/or non-weight bearing orders for lower limbs at time of eligibility.
* Life expectancy \<180 days due to chronic medical condition (per judgement of clinical team).
* Limitation in use of life support (excluding a sole "No CPR/DNR" order) at time of eligibility.
* Death deemed inevitable due to severity of critical illness at time of eligibility (per clinical team).
* Unable to understand/communicate in English.
* Not the first ICU admission during the index hospital admission.
* More than 72 hours since meeting all eligibility (to allow potential for early intervention).
